metadata.title: Stability for the Bray-Brendle-Neves Scalar Sphere Rigidity Theorem
metadata.abstract: Let $(M^3,g)$ be a closed and oriented 3-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $\pi_2(M)\neq 0$ and let $A_{\pi_2}(M,g)$ denote the least area among homotopically nontrivial two-spheres in $M$. By a theorem of Bray-Brendle-Neves, $A_{\pi_2}(M,g)\inf_M R_g \leq 8\pi$ with equality characterizing the cylindrical geometry $S^2\times\mathbb{R}$. Motivated by Sormani's questions on volume preserving intrinsic flat stability for scalar curvature rigidity problems, we study the almost equality regime of this theorem. We build, using Sweeney's tunnel construction, a sequence satisfying $A_{\pi_2}(M_j,g_j)\inf_{M_j} R_{g_j} \rightarrow 8\pi$ with uniformly bounded volume and diameter whose volume preserving intrinsic flat limit is not the Bray-Brendle-Neves rigidity space, showing that stability fails in general. We then prove stability in two special cases: for sequences of rotationally symmetric metrics (with non-collapsing assumptions) and for sequences of manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature.
